data.cultural_impact: The name Meliora, being of Latin origin, connects to the rich history and cultural influence of the Roman civilization. This name represents the aspiration for personal and societal advancement and improvement, echoing the values of resilience and progression that have been passed down through history.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Meliora represents the constant striving towards personal improvement, mirroring the idea of growth and transformation in various religious beliefs and philosophies. It is a reminder that we all have the potential to be better versions of ourselves and can inspire those around us to do the same. Furthermore, the name can be seen as an answer to the question posed by St. Augustine, "Deus creavit nos ut ipsos feremus; fit Si Deus nos ne crearet, non feremus," which translates to "God created us to carry Him; but were it not God who carried us, we would not be able to carry Him." (sic) This name reminds us of the support and strength that we can draw from our faith and the belief in a higher power that can help us to continually become "more excellent" beings.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, the name Meliora was given to a 13th century nun who lived in the Monastery of the Holy Cross in Prague. She was renowned for her exceptional virtues, beauty, and piety. Her name is said to have been derived from the Latin word 'melior', meaning 'better' or 'more excellent'.
historical_references.context: Legendary account of a holy nun in Prague

historical_references.reference: The name Meliora was also the title of a 17th century English poem by Robert Herrick. In the poem, Meliora represents the idea of happiness and joy, especially in the context of the harvest festival. The poem's opening line reads: 'Now welcome, Meliora, fair and sweet, Thou goddess of our rustic rites, And thou that art our autumn's heat, With maturing crops and ripe delights.'
historical_references.context: Title of an English poem by Robert Herrick on the theme of happiness and joy associated with harvest festival
